event_overview.subject: Kim's visit to China is his latest move in an increasingly assertive foreign policy as he seeks to align Pyongyang with Beijing and Moscow i
event_overview.summary: This event is Kim Jong Un’s one-day visit to Dandong, China, on October 24, 2026, where he met senior Chinese official Wang Huning, visited a Korean War memorial and crossed the newly opened China-DPRK Yalu River bridge. Chinese state media framed the trip around commemorating Chinese forces’ entry into the Korean War and advancing longstanding China–North Korea friendship and practical cooperation.

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: Kim visited Dandong, Liaoning Province, in northeastern China, on October 24, 2026.

facts.label: Participants
facts.value: Kim was received and accompanied by Wang Huning, a member of the Communist Party of China Politburo Standing Committee and chairman of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference National Committee.

facts.label: Stated purpose
facts.value: The visit included a tribute at Dandong’s Memorial Hall of the War to Resist U.S. Aggression and Aid Korea, ahead of the 76th anniversary of the Chinese People’s Volunteers entering the Korean War.

facts.label: Border link
facts.value: The New China-DPRK Yalu River Bridge connects Dandong with Sinuiju, North Korea; it officially opened to traffic on October 15, 2026, after a long delay.

facts.label: Stated cooperation aim
facts.value: Chinese officials described the bridge as infrastructure intended to facilitate bilateral trade and people-to-people exchanges; during the visit, both sides expressed support for expanding practical cooperation.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the October 24–25, 2026 visit and bridge-related diplomacy, not the full history of China–North Korea relations or North Korea’s wider relationships with Russia and other states.
